intent.raw_query: Tokyo city break, $3000 for couple, food and tech culture, April 2026 from SFO

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and street snacks from local vendors. This iconic food destination offers an authentic taste of Tokyo's culinary culture, with vendors who have perfected their craft over generations. Ideal for food lovers wanting to experience the heart of Tokyo's seafood and street food scene.

experiences.name: Odaiba Waterfront Tech & Culture Day
experiences.description: Spend a day at Odaiba, a futuristic artificial island on Tokyo Bay with a beachfront setting. Visit teamLab Borderless digital art museum, explore the Toyota Mega Web showroom, and enjoy the beach promenade with views of Rainbow Bridge. This area perfectly blends tech culture, modern art, and a rare Tokyo beachfront experience.

experiences.name: Akihabara Electric Town Deep Dive
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Tokyo's legendary electronics and otaku culture district. Browse multi-story electronics shops, retro game stores, anime merchandise outlets, and visit hands-on tech showrooms. Experience maid cafes, arcade gaming floors, and cutting-edge gadget stores that define Japan's global tech identity.

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple & Asakusa Cultural Walk
experiences.description: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple, Senso-ji, in the historic Asakusa district. Stroll through the Nakamise shopping street for traditional crafts and snacks, participate in omikuji fortune drawing, and observe traditional ceremonies. The area offers a vivid contrast to modern Tokyo and a deep dive into Edo-period culture.

experiences.name: Ramen & Izakaya Night Experience in Shinjuku
experiences.description: Spend an evening exploring Shinjuku's vibrant food alleys, including the famous Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane). Enjoy a steaming bowl of authentic Tokyo-style ramen, then hop between traditional izakayas for yakitori, edamame, and local sake. This experience captures the soul of Tokyo's nighttime local food culture in a lively urban setting.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Tokyo
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and prepare for arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Narita or Haneda Airport at 13:00. Take the budget-friendly Airport Limousine Bus or train (Keikyu Line from Haneda ~600 JPY, or Narita Express ~3,000 JPY) to Tsukiji area. Check in to your boutique stay in Tsukiji, Chuo City. Freshen up and take a short orientation walk around the Tsukiji Outer Market neighborhood to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Tsukiji Outer Market stalls for a casual evening snack-style dinner — try tamagoyaki (sweet egg omelet), fresh sushi sets, and grilled seafood skewers from market vendors. Walk along the Sumida River waterfront at dusk for a relaxing first evening in Tokyo.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or grab a quick convenience store bento (7-Eleven, Lawson, or FamilyMart) near the airport for ~500–700 JPY
meals.dinner: Tsukiji Outer Market food stalls — budget ~1,000–1,500 JPY for a mix of street snacks and a sushi set

day_by_day.notes: Buy a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport for easy train and bus travel throughout your stay. Keep Day 1 light — jet lag is real. The Tsukiji Outer Market stalls typically close by 17:00–18:00, so head there promptly after check-in.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early (5:30–6:00 AM) to visit Tsukiji Outer Market at its liveliest — enjoy a classic Tokyo breakfast of fresh tuna sashimi, tamago sushi, and miso soup from the market vendors. Browse the kitchen tool and dried goods shops that line the lanes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short subway ride to Hamarikyu Gardens (entry ~300 JPY) — a beautiful traditional Japanese garden with a teahouse on a tidal pond, surrounded by city skyscrapers. Then head to Ginza for window shopping and people-watching along Chuo-dori. Visit the free Itoya stationery flagship store — a fascinating 12-floor stationery wonderland reflecting Japanese design culture.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shiodome or Shimbashi area for dinner. Explore the Shimbashi salaryman izakaya alleys for cheap set meals. Then stroll back along the waterfront to your hotel.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market — fresh sushi breakfast set ~800–1,200 JPY
meals.lunch: Hamarikyu teahouse matcha and wagashi (Japanese sweets) ~800 JPY, or a convenience store lunch
meals.dinner: Shimbashi izakaya — teishoku (set meal) with rice, miso soup, and a main dish ~800–1,200 JPY

day_by_day.notes: Hamarikyu Gardens is especially beautiful in spring with cherry blossoms and wisteria. Ginza is expensive to shop but completely free to explore. Shimbashi is one of Tokyo's best areas for authentic, affordable salaryman dining.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Asakusa (about 20 minutes from Tsukiji). Visit Senso-ji Temple — Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple — free entry. Explore Nakamise-dori shopping street for traditional souvenirs, ningyo-yaki cakes, and senbei rice crackers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the nearby Asakusa Culture Tourist Information Center for a free rooftop view over Senso-ji and the Skytree. Then explore Kappabashi 'Kitchen Town' — a fascinating street of professional kitchen supply stores, plastic food displays, and chef's tools, all free to browse. Great insight into Japan's food culture.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Tokyo Skytree (optional, ~2,100 JPY for lower deck) for panoramic city views at dusk. Alternatively, enjoy the view for free from the base plaza area. Dine in the Asakusa or Oshiage neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or hotel — ~400–600 JPY
meals.lunch: Asakusa ramen shop or tempura tendon restaurant — ~800–1,000 JPY
meals.dinner: Oshiage neighborhood izakaya or Asakusa yakitori stall — ~1,000–1,500 JPY

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is free but very crowded on weekends — arriving early on a weekday morning is ideal. Kappabashi is a unique Tokyo experience that perfectly blends food culture and Japanese craftsmanship — don't miss the giant golden chef head on one of the buildings.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Akihabara — Tokyo's legendary Electric Town and the global epicenter of tech and otaku culture. Explore multi-floor electronics stores like Yodobashi Akiba (free entry), retro game shops, anime merchandise stores, and the famous Akihabara Radio Center for vintage electronics parts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the free floors of Yodobashi Camera to marvel at the latest Japanese tech gadgets, appliances, and audio equipment. Explore the retro gaming floors of Super Potato and other used game stores. Check out the maid café culture (budget tip: just observe the exterior or take a photo — full maid café experiences cost ~1,500–2,000 JPY).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Akihabara's neon-lit streets after dark — the area transforms into a glowing spectacle. Grab dinner at one of the many affordable chain restaurants in the area.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store near hotel — ~400–600 JPY
meals.lunch: Akihabara — Japanese curry at CoCo Ichibanya or a ramen chain ~700–1,000 JPY
meals.dinner: Yoshinoya, Matsuya, or Sukiya gyudon (beef bowl) chain near Akihabara station — ~500–700 JPY

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is a must for tech and culture enthusiasts. Saturday afternoons can be very crowded. The free floors of electronics megastores are endlessly fascinating even without buying anything. Budget tip: used game and electronics stores often have incredible deals.

day_by_day.morning: Take the train to Harajuku. Visit Meiji Jingu Shrine — a serene forested Shinto shrine in the heart of the city, free entry. Walk the long gravel path through the towering torii gate and forest — a peaceful contrast to the urban buzz.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down Takeshita Street in Harajuku for Tokyo's famous youth fashion, crepes, and quirky pop culture shops. Then stroll along Omotesando Boulevard — Tokyo's elegant tree-lined avenue — for free architecture gazing (Tadao Ando's Omotesando Hills, etc.). Head to Shibuya and witness the famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the Shibuya Scramble from the free observation area at Mag's Park (Shibuya 109-2 building rooftop) or the Starbucks at Tsutaya. Explore Shibuya's side streets for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Harajuku area bakery or convenience store — ~400–700 JPY
meals.lunch: Harajuku crepe (~500 JPY) plus a snack from Takeshita Street stalls
meals.dinner: Shibuya — ichiran solo ramen booth ~890–1,200 JPY (a classic Tokyo experience)

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Jingu is free and one of the most spiritual and atmospheric spots in Tokyo. Takeshita Street is a fascinating window into Japanese youth culture. The Shibuya Scramble is best experienced both from ground level and from above.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the free teamLab Digital Art Museum preview or explore Odaiba — Tokyo's futuristic artificial island in Tokyo Bay. Take the Yurikamome monorail (~320 JPY) from Shimbashi for great views of Rainbow Bridge. Visit the free DiverCity Tokyo Plaza and see the giant Gundam RX-78-2 statue outside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Miraikan (National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation) in Odaiba — entry ~630 JPY. This museum perfectly blends tech culture with futurism, featuring robots, space exhibits, and interactive science displays. Visit the free floor exhibits at Fuji TV building.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset over Tokyo Bay from Odaiba's waterfront promenade with a view of Rainbow Bridge and the city skyline. Return to Tsukiji for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store near hotel — ~400–600 JPY
meals.lunch: Odaiba DiverCity food court — ramen or Japanese set meal ~800–1,000 JPY
meals.dinner: Back in Tsukiji/Ginza area — conveyor belt sushi (kaiten-zushi) at Sushiro or Kura Sushi ~1,000–1,500 JPY

day_by_day.notes: Miraikan is one of Tokyo's best budget-friendly tech experiences — highly recommended for tech culture enthusiasts. The Odaiba waterfront is especially beautiful at sunset and after dark with Rainbow Bridge illuminated.

day_by_day.morning: Take the train to Shinjuku. Visit the free Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck (open from 9:00 AM) on the 45th floor for a 360-degree panoramic view of Tokyo — one of the best free views in the city, including Mt. Fuji on clear days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden (entry ~500 JPY) — one of Japan's most beautiful parks, a perfect mix of Japanese, French, and English garden styles. Then explore the labyrinthine Shinjuku underground shopping arcades and the famous Takashimaya Times Square department store basement food hall (depachika) — free to browse and sample.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Shinjuku's Golden Gai — a network of tiny atmospheric bars in narrow alleys. Budget tip: walk through and absorb the atmosphere for free, or choose one small bar for a single drink (~600–800 JPY). Then explore the neon spectacle of Kabukicho entertainment district.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or Shinjuku station bakery — ~400–600 JPY
meals.lunch: Shinjuku Gyoen picnic — buy onigiri, sandwiches, and snacks from a nearby convenience store ~500–700 JPY
meals.dinner: Shinjuku — standing sushi bar or ramen alley (Shinjuku Ramen Street) ~700–1,000 JPY

day_by_day.notes: The Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck is completely free — one of the best budget tips in Tokyo. The south tower is open in the evenings too. Shinjuku Gyoen is one of the finest gardens in Japan and perfect for a midday rest.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Yanaka — one of Tokyo's best-preserved old shitamachi (downtown) neighborhoods. Explore Yanaka Cemetery with its tree-lined paths and historic graves, and browse Yanaka Ginza shopping street for traditional crafts, local snacks, and artisan shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Nezu and Sendagi area nearby. Visit Nezu Shrine — a smaller but stunning vermillion torii-lined shrine path similar to Kyoto's Fushimi Inari, and it's completely free. Browse the charming indie bookshops and cafes in the Yanesen (Yanaka-Nezu-Sendagi) neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Tokyo. Head to Ueno for an evening stroll through Ueno Park and a visit to Ameyoko Market — a lively outdoor market street with cheap food, clothing, and goods. Great for budget souvenir shopping.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store near hotel — ~400–600 JPY
meals.lunch: Yanaka Ginza — menchi katsu (fried meat cutlet) croquette ~150–200 JPY, plus other street snacks ~600–800 JPY total
meals.dinner: Ameyoko Market food stalls — gyoza, skewers, or a cheap sushi set ~800–1,200 JPY

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is one of the most authentic and atmospheric neighborhoods in Tokyo — a window into pre-war Tokyo life. Nezu Shrine is a hidden gem that avoids the massive crowds of Fushimi Inari in Kyoto. Ameyoko is loud, vibrant, and very budget-friendly.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ueno — start at the Tokyo National Museum (entry ~1,000 JPY) — Japan's largest museum with an incredible collection of samurai armor, ancient pottery, Buddhist sculpture, and ukiyo-e woodblock prints. A must for culture enthusiasts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the rest of Ueno Park — visit the free Shinobazu Pond and its lotus-covered waters, the Ueno Toshogu Shrine (free exterior), and browse the weekend art market stalls. Then walk to nearby Akihabara for a second, more focused exploration of a specific interest — vintage electronics, retro games, or anime figure stores.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tsukiji area for a relaxing evening. Visit the Tsukiji Hongan-ji Temple — a stunning Indo-Saracenic style Buddhist temple near your hotel, free to enter. Quiet evening dinner near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or hotel — ~400–600 JPY
meals.lunch: Ueno Park area — udon or soba restaurant ~700–900 JPY
meals.dinner: Tsukiji neighborhood — local soba or donburi restaurant ~800–1,000 JPY

day_by_day.notes: The Tokyo National Museum is one of the world's great museums and excellent value at 1,000 JPY. Tsukiji Hongan-ji is an architecturally unique and often overlooked gem right near your hotel — worth a quiet evening visit.

day_by_day.morning: Take the train to Shimokitazawa — Tokyo's beloved bohemian neighborhood known for vintage fashion, indie music venues, and a creative counterculture vibe. Browse the many vintage clothing stores (rag & bone, New York Joe Exchange) and independent record shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Shimokitazawa's charming narrow streets, indie cafes, and second-hand bookshops. Then head to nearby Nakameguro — walk along the Meguro River canal, lined with cherry trees (beautiful in spring). Browse the stylish boutiques and independent shops along the river.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Daikanyama — Tokyo's upscale but walkable neighborhood. Visit the stunning Daikanyama T-Site (Tsutaya Books) — a beautifully designed bookstore and cultural hub, free to browse. Return to Shibuya or Tsukiji for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store near hotel — ~400–600 JPY
meals.lunch: Shimokitazawa — curry rice at a local indie restaurant ~700–900 JPY
meals.dinner: Nakameguro or Shibuya — affordable ramen or Japanese home-style cooking restaurant ~800–1,200 JPY

day_by_day.notes: Shimokitazawa is the antithesis of mainstream Tokyo and offers a fascinating look at Tokyo's underground creative culture. Daikanyama T-Site is architecturally stunning and culturally rich — a perfect example of how Japan elevates everyday spaces into art.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ikebukuro — explore Sunshine City complex and the free observation areas. Head to the massive Bic Camera electronics store for the latest Japanese tech, cameras, and gadgets. Explore the Otome Road area (Ikebukuro's version of Akihabara, focused on manga and anime for a different demographic).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the free Rikkyo University campus — a beautiful Gothic brick campus reminiscent of an English university, surprisingly photogenic. Then head to Mejiro or Otsuka for a quieter, more local neighborhood exploration — a glimpse of everyday Tokyo life away from tourist crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tsukiji for a special farewell-style dinner at a proper sushi restaurant. Tsukiji area has excellent mid-range sushi restaurants that offer quality fish at reasonable prices given the proximity to the former wholesale market.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store — ~400–600 JPY
meals.lunch: Ikebukuro — tonkatsu (pork cutlet) set meal at a local restaurant ~900–1,200 JPY
meals.dinner: Tsukiji area sushi restaurant — omakase lunch-style dinner or nigiri set ~1,500–2,500 JPY (a budget splurge worth it)

day_by_day.notes: Ikebukuro is often overlooked by tourists but is one of Tokyo's most interesting and authentic commercial districts. The Tsukiji area dinner is a fitting budget splurge — you're staying in one of Tokyo's best neighborhoods for fresh seafood, so take advantage of it.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Koishikawa Korakuen Garden (entry ~300 JPY) — one of Tokyo's oldest and most beautiful traditional Japanese gardens, near Tokyo Dome. Then explore the Jimbocho neighborhood — Tokyo's famous used bookstore district with hundreds of second-hand bookshops, antique map sellers, and academic publishers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Kanda Myojin Shrine — a historic Shinto shrine closely associated with Tokyo's tech and IT culture (many tech companies come here for blessings). The shrine sells unique IT-themed ema (prayer plaques) and omamori (charms) — fascinating intersection of tradition and tech. Then explore Ochanomizu's music instrument street.
day_by_day.evening: Final big evening in Tokyo — head to Roppongi for a walk through the art district. Visit the free outdoor sculpture garden of Mori Art Museum (the museum itself costs ~1,800 JPY — optional). Enjoy Tokyo Midtown's free outdoor illuminations and gardens.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store — ~400–600 JPY
meals.lunch: Jimbocho area — old-school Japanese restaurant or soba shop ~700–900 JPY
meals.dinner: Roppongi or Azabu area — don't be deterred by the upscale reputation; find a local ramen or gyoza restaurant in the side streets ~800–1,200 JPY

day_by_day.notes: Kanda Myojin's connection to IT and tech culture is a uniquely Tokyo experience — the shrine even has an official IT industry prayer service. Jimbocho is paradise for book lovers and history enthusiasts. This is a good day for final souvenir shopping in Jimbocho.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo — return to Tsukiji Outer Market for one last breakfast of fresh sushi and tamagoyaki, completing the full circle from Day 1. Browse any remaining market stalls for last-minute food souvenirs (dried seaweed, dashi packs, Japanese knives if budget allows).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time: visit the nearby Hamarikyu Gardens one final time for a peaceful farewell stroll, or do any last-minute shopping at the Ginza area. Pack up and check out of the hotel. Head to the airport via train or bus.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. If evening flight: spend remaining time in Ginza or at a nearby depachika (department store basement food hall) for last food purchases and a final meal.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market — final sushi breakfast ~1,000–1,500 JPY
meals.lunch: Ginza depachika or convenience store — ~600–900 JPY
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or final meal near hotel before departure — ~1,000–1,500 JPY

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for airport travel and check-in. Narita is about 60–90 minutes from central Tokyo; Haneda is about 30–45 minutes. Buy any last food souvenirs at Tsukiji or a depachika — Japanese snacks, tea, and condiments make excellent budget-friendly gifts. Don't forget to return your Suica card at the airport for a refund of the 500 JPY deposit.

trip_options.title: Classic Tokyo Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and take the Narita Express or Limousine Bus to Tsukiji area (approx. 60–90 min). Check in to your Tsukiji boutique stay and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a gentle orientation stroll around Tsukiji Outer Market (仲見世通り周辺). Browse the fresh seafood stalls, kitchen tool shops, and street snack vendors. Pick up tamagoyaki (sweet egg omelette) or fresh oysters from a vendor to snack on and get your bearings in the neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a local izakaya near Tsukiji. Try Tsukiji Itadori or a similar mid-range neighborhood spot for grilled fish, sashimi sets, and cold Sapporo beer. Wind down early to recover from jet lag.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: Grab a bento or onigiri at the airport or convenience store (7-Eleven / FamilyMart) en route to hotel
meals.dinner: Local izakaya near Tsukiji — sashimi platter + grilled skewers, approx. ¥2,500–¥3,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Priority on Day 1 is rest and light acclimatization. Avoid heavy sightseeing to counter jet lag. Purchase a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport for seamless transit throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day early at Tsukiji Outer Market (opens ~5:00 AM, best visited 7:00–9:00 AM). Join locals and chefs shopping for the freshest tuna, uni, and seasonal produce. Enjoy a classic Tsukiji breakfast: a bowl of fresh tuna don or clam miso soup at one of the market's iconic breakfast counters such as Yonehana or Nakaya.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi to Hamarikyu Gardens (浜離宮恩賜庭園), a stunning Edo-era tidal garden with a traditional teahouse on the water. Enjoy matcha and wagashi (Japanese sweets) at the Nakajima no Ochaya teahouse. Afterward, stroll along the Sumida River waterfront toward Ginza.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Ginza (銀座) for its blend of high-end culture and accessible street life. Visit the Itoya stationery flagship store and browse the Ginza Six atrium. Dinner at Ginza Nair's (legendary Indian-Japanese fusion, affordable for Ginza) or try a tonkatsu set at Ginza Bairin.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market — fresh tuna don or tamagoyaki sandwich, approx. ¥800–¥1,200
meals.lunch: Light snack at Hamarikyu teahouse — matcha + wagashi set, approx. ¥800
meals.dinner: Ginza mid-range restaurant — tonkatsu or fusion set meal, approx. ¥2,000–¥3,500

day_by_day.notes: Hamarikyu Gardens entry fee: ¥300. Tsukiji Inner Market tuna auctions require advance lottery registration — the Outer Market is freely accessible. Wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Asakusa (浅草) via subway (15 min from Tsukiji). Visit Senso-ji Temple at opening time for a serene atmosphere before crowds arrive. Draw an omikuji (fortune slip), browse Nakamise-dori shopping street for traditional crafts, fans, and ningyo-yaki cakes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Tokyo Skytree (東京スカイツリー) — a 10-minute stroll from Asakusa. Ascend to the Tembo Deck (350m) for panoramic views of Tokyo. On clear spring days, you may spot cherry blossom remnants and Mount Fuji. Explore the Solamachi shopping complex at the base for Japanese design goods and snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward Akihabara (秋葉原) — the heart of Tokyo's tech and otaku culture (20 min by subway). Explore multi-floor electronics stores like Yodobashi Camera, retro game shops, and anime merchandise floors. Dinner at a themed cafe or a reliable ramen shop such as Fuunji-style tsukemen in the area.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby café — Japanese-style toast set, approx. ¥600–¥900
meals.lunch: Solamachi food hall at Skytree base — gyoza, takoyaki, or soba, approx. ¥1,000–¥1,500
meals.dinner: Akihabara ramen or curry house — approx. ¥1,000–¥1,800

day_by_day.notes: Skytree Tembo Deck tickets: approx. ¥2,100 adult. Book online in advance to skip queues. Akihabara is best explored in the evening when neon lights are fully lit and shops are busiest.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Shibuya (渋谷). Start at the famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing — experience the organized chaos from street level, then head to Mag's Park or Shibuya Sky observation deck for an aerial view. Visit the Hachiko statue for a cultural moment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Harajuku (原宿) and Takeshita Street for youth fashion, crepe stands, and quirky pop culture. Then walk through Omotesando (表参道) — Tokyo's tree-lined 'Champs-Élysées' — for architecture, concept stores, and Japanese designer boutiques. Visit the Omotesando Hills complex designed by Tadao Ando.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Daikanyama (代官山) for a quieter, sophisticated evening. Browse the iconic Tsutaya Books (代官山 蔦屋書店) — a beautifully designed bookstore-café hybrid that represents Tokyo's fusion of design and culture. Dinner at a neighborhood bistro or Japanese-French fusion restaurant in Daikanyama.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or hotel — onigiri + coffee, approx. ¥400–¥600
meals.lunch: Harajuku crepe + snacks on Takeshita Street, approx. ¥800–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Daikanyama bistro or izakaya — approx. ¥2,500–¥4,000

day_by_day.notes: Shibuya Sky observation deck: approx. ¥2,000. Saturday crowds in Harajuku are lively — arrive before noon for a better experience. Tsutaya Books in Daikanyama is open until midnight.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Meiji Shrine (明治神宮) in Harajuku for a peaceful forest walk through 70,000 trees. Witness a traditional Shinto ceremony if timing aligns (Sunday mornings are common). Explore the inner garden and iris garden (¥500 entry, beautiful in spring).
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel to Shinjuku (新宿). Explore Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden (新宿御苑) — one of Tokyo's largest parks and a prime cherry blossom / spring greenery spot (¥500 entry). Afterward, explore the Shinjuku government building observation deck (free) for city views.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Shinjuku's legendary nightlife district. Walk through Kabukicho (歌舞伎町) and Golden Gai (黄金街) — a maze of tiny atmospheric bars, each seating 5–8 people, many welcoming to tourists. Have drinks at 2–3 Golden Gai bars (cover charge ¥500–¥1,000 per bar). Dinner at a yakitori alley (思い出横丁 Memory Lane).

meals.breakfast: Hotel or local bakery near Tsukiji — croissant + coffee
meals.lunch: Shinjuku Gyoen picnic-style — pick up bento from a nearby convenience store or depachika (department store basement food hall), approx. ¥800–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Memory Lane (Omoide Yokocho) yakitori skewers + beer, approx. ¥1,500–¥2,500

day_by_day.notes: Shinjuku Gyoen is alcohol-free. Golden Gai bars are cash-only — carry ¥5,000–¥10,000 in small bills. Some bars have a 'regulars only' policy but most welcome tourists with a friendly knock.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated tech culture day. Start at the teamLab Planets TOKYO (チームラボ プラネッツ) in Toyosu — an immersive digital art experience blending technology, nature, and culture. Book tickets online in advance (approx. ¥3,200). Open from 9:00 AM.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Odaiba (お台場) via the Yurikamome monorail — enjoy futuristic waterfront views. Visit the Miraikan (日本科学未来館 — National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation) to explore robots, AI, space tech, and interactive science exhibits. Meet ASIMO-style robots and explore Japan's vision of the future.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Odaiba for sunset over Tokyo Bay and Rainbow Bridge. Explore DiverCity Tokyo Plaza and its iconic life-size Gundam statue (free). Dinner at Decks Tokyo Beach food court or a waterfront restaurant with bay views.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby café
meals.lunch: Toyosu Market area — fresh seafood bowl at Senkyaku Banrai food hall, approx. ¥1,500–¥2,500
meals.dinner: Odaiba waterfront restaurant or food court — ramen, sushi, or international options, approx. ¥1,500–¥2,500

day_by_day.notes: teamLab Planets tickets sell out weeks in advance — book online before your trip. Miraikan entry: approx. ¥630. The Yurikamome monorail offers great views of the bay and is covered by Suica card.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko (日光) — a UNESCO World Heritage mountain shrine complex 2 hours from Tokyo by Tobu Nikko Line (approx. ¥1,360 one way). Depart by 8:00 AM. Explore Tosho-gu Shrine, the ornate mausoleum of Tokugawa Ieyasu, surrounded by cedar forests and cascading waterfalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko — walk to Kegon Falls (華厳の滝), one of Japan's most spectacular waterfalls, and stroll along Lake Chuzenji (中禅寺湖) for mountain scenery. Enjoy the peaceful contrast to urban Tokyo.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Relax near Tsukiji — pick up fresh sushi or a bento from the Tsukiji market area for a low-key dinner at the hotel or nearby.

meals.breakfast: Early convenience store breakfast before departure — onigiri + coffee, approx. ¥400
meals.lunch: Nikko local restaurant — yuba (tofu skin) cuisine, a Nikko specialty, approx. ¥1,200–¥2,000
meals.dinner: Tsukiji takeaway sushi or soba restaurant near hotel, approx. ¥1,500–¥2,500

day_by_day.notes: Purchase the Tobu Nikko All Area Pass (approx. ¥4,520) for unlimited buses and trains within Nikko. Wear sturdy shoes for temple paths. Tosho-gu entry: approx. ¥1,300. Depart Tokyo no later than 8:00 AM to maximize time in Nikko.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Yanaka (谷中) — one of Tokyo's best-preserved old shitamachi (downtown) neighborhoods that survived WWII bombing. Wander Yanaka Cemetery (beautiful in spring with blooming trees), browse Yanaka Ginza shotengai (shopping street) for handmade crafts, pickles, and traditional snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Nezu Shrine (根津神社) — a stunning vermilion torii gate tunnel shrine, less crowded than Fushimi Inari in Kyoto. Nearby, visit the Nezu Museum (根津美術館) in Omotesando for a world-class collection of pre-modern Asian art in a serene garden setting (approx. ¥1,300).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Ueno (上野) for the evening. Explore Ameyoko Market (アメ横) — a lively open-air market street with street food, clothing, and fresh produce. Dinner at one of Ueno's many affordable izakayas or Korean BBQ restaurants near the market.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Yanaka bakery — local melon pan or cream bread
meals.lunch: Yanaka Ginza street food — menchi katsu (fried minced meat cutlet) + canned coffee, approx. ¥600–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Ueno izakaya or Ameyoko area Korean BBQ — approx. ¥2,000–¥3,000

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is best explored on foot — wear comfortable shoes. The neighborhood has excellent independent coffee shops and antique stores. Nezu Shrine's azalea festival (Bunkyo Azalea Festival) often runs in mid-April — check if it coincides with your visit.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tokyo National Museum (東京国立博物館) in Ueno Park — Japan's largest and oldest museum with an extraordinary collection of samurai armor, Buddhist sculpture, ukiyo-e woodblock prints, and ancient ceramics. Entry: approx. ¥1,000. Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel to Akihabara for a deeper tech culture dive. Visit the Radio Kaikan building (8 floors of electronics, model kits, and collectibles), explore the Super Potato retro gaming store, and browse the latest gadgets at Yodobashi Akiba. Optional: visit a maid café for a uniquely Japanese pop-culture experience.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Kanda (神田) and Jimbocho (神保町) — Tokyo's legendary used bookstore district. Browse hundreds of specialty bookshops for vintage manga, Japanese woodblock prints, and rare publications. Dinner at a classic Kanda restaurant — try Kanda Yabu Soba (founded 1880) for premium hand-cut soba noodles.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or nearby café — Japanese breakfast set
meals.lunch: Ueno Park area bento or museum café — approx. ¥1,000–¥1,500
meals.dinner: Kanda Yabu Soba or similar heritage soba restaurant — approx. ¥1,500–¥2,500

day_by_day.notes: Tokyo National Museum is closed on Mondays. Maid café experiences typically cost ¥1,500–¥3,000 including a drink. Jimbocho bookstores are mostly open until 6:00–7:00 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Half-day trip to Kamakura (鎌倉) — 1 hour from Tokyo by JR Yokosuka Line. Visit the Great Buddha (Kotoku-in Daibutsu, ¥300) and Hase-dera Temple with its stunning hillside gardens and sea views. Explore Komachi-dori street for artisan shops and matcha desserts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue in Kamakura — hike the Daibutsu Hiking Trail through bamboo groves and forest shrines back toward Kita-Kamakura station. Visit Engaku-ji Temple, a serene Zen complex. Return to Tokyo by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Spend the evening in Roppongi (六本木) — Tokyo's international arts and nightlife district. Visit the Mori Art Museum (森美術館) on the 53rd floor of Roppongi Hills — the attached Tokyo City View observation deck offers spectacular nighttime panoramas (entry: approx. ¥2,000). Dinner at a mid-range restaurant in Roppongi Hills.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast or train station convenience store
meals.lunch: Kamakura — shirasu don (whitebait rice bowl, a local specialty) at a restaurant near Hase station, approx. ¥1,200–¥1,800
meals.dinner: Roppongi Hills restaurant — Japanese fusion or international cuisine, approx. ¥3,000–¥4,500

day_by_day.notes: Kamakura is a popular day trip — depart Tokyo before 9:00 AM on weekdays to beat crowds. The Daibutsu Hiking Trail takes approx. 1.5 hours and involves some steep sections. Mori Art Museum is open until 10:00 PM on Fridays.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Tsukiji Fish Market area one more time for a proper breakfast at a sit-down sushi counter — try Sushi Dai or Daiwa Sushi (arrive early, expect a queue) for the omakase breakfast set (approx. ¥4,000–¥5,000 — a splurge worth having). Afterward, explore the Nihonbashi (日本橋) historic district nearby.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Nihonbashi Mitsukoshi department store — Japan's oldest department store (founded 1673). Visit its basement depachika food hall — a world-class showcase of Japanese culinary culture with artisan wagashi, bento, sushi, and seasonal delicacies. Head to the Coredo Muromachi complex for traditional craft and design shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Evening food tour of Shibuya's hidden dining scene — explore Nonbei Yokocho (ノンベイ横丁, 'Drunkard's Alley') in Shibuya for intimate bar-hopping. Then try the Shibuya Parco basement for contemporary Japanese food hall dining. End the evening at a standing sushi bar (tachigui sushi) for a final round.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji sushi counter omakase — approx. ¥4,000–¥5,000 (splurge meal)
meals.lunch: Nihonbashi depachika — curated bento or wagashi tasting, approx. ¥1,200–¥2,000
meals.dinner: Shibuya Nonbei Yokocho bar-hopping + standing sushi — approx. ¥2,500–¥4,000

day_by_day.notes: Sushi Dai and Daiwa Sushi queues can be 1–2 hours — arrive by 6:30 AM for a reasonable wait. Alternatively, book a counter seat at a mid-range sushi restaurant via Tableall or Omakase booking platforms. Nonbei Yokocho bars are mostly cash-only.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Shibuya's cutting-edge tech and culture hub — explore the newly developed Shibuya Stream and Scramble Square complexes. Head to the Shibuya Innovation Base or drop into one of the area's concept stores showcasing Japanese tech design. Visit Loft or Tokyu Hands for innovative Japanese lifestyle products and gadgets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Nakameguro (中目黒) — walk along the Meguro River canal, lined with cherry trees (beautiful even post-bloom with fresh green leaves). Browse the independent boutiques, vintage shops, and design studios along the canal. Visit the Starbucks Reserve Roastery Tokyo (スターバックス リザーブ ロースタリー) — a stunning architectural coffee experience.
day_by_day.evening: Final major dinner — treat yourself to a memorable meal. Book in advance at a mid-range omakase kaiseki restaurant in Ginza or Nihonbashi (approx. ¥8,000–¥12,000 per person for a multi-course Japanese dinner). This is the ideal night for a cultural fine dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Nakameguro café or hotel — specialty coffee + toast
meals.lunch: Nakameguro canal-side café or bistro — pasta or Japanese lunch set, approx. ¥1,200–¥1,800
meals.dinner: Kaiseki or omakase restaurant — approx. ¥8,000–¥12,000 (special occasion splurge)

day_by_day.notes: Starbucks Reserve Roastery Tokyo is extremely popular — visit on a Sunday afternoon and expect a wait. Book the kaiseki dinner at least 2–3 weeks in advance via Tableall, Omakase.jp, or Gurunavi. Nakameguro is best explored on foot.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo. Return to Tsukiji Outer Market one last time for a farewell breakfast — fresh uni (sea urchin) on rice or a tamago sando (egg sandwich). Pick up last-minute food souvenirs: dashi packets, matcha, wasabi, and premium soy sauce from the market stalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time — visit a nearby convenience store (7-Eleven or Lawson) for final Japanese snack haul (KitKat flavors, Pocky, onigiri). Pack and check out of the hotel. Head to the airport via Narita Express or Limousine Bus (allow 90–120 min from Tsukiji area).
day_by_day.evening: Departure. If time permits before leaving, enjoy one final bowl of ramen at Tokyo Station's Ramen Street (東京ラーメンストリート) in the basement — a fitting farewell to Tokyo's food culture.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market — fresh seafood breakfast, approx. ¥1,000–¥1,800
meals.lunch: Light — convenience store snacks or Tokyo Station food stalls, approx. ¥500–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Tokyo Station Ramen Street or airport restaurant, approx. ¥1,000–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00 AM — store luggage at the hotel or at a coin locker at Tokyo Station (¥500–¥900/day). Return your Suica card at the airport for a refund of remaining balance (minus ¥220 handling fee). Allow ample time for airport security and immigration.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Tokyo Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and street snacks from local vendors. This iconic food destination offers an authentic taste of Tokyo's culinary culture, with vendors who have perfected their craft over generations. Ideal for food lovers wanting to experience the heart of Tokyo's seafood and street food scene.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Narita/Haneda Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private airport transfer arranged via luxury car service (e.g., Hinomaru Limousine) to boutique hotel in Tsukiji, Chuo City. Check-in, freshen up, and settle in.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation stroll through Tsukiji Outer Market (a short walk from the hotel). Browse the iconic stalls selling fresh seafood, pickles, tamagoyaki, and Japanese kitchenware. Sample street snacks including freshly grilled scallops, uni on rice crackers, and matcha soft-serve. Visit Namiyoke Inari Shrine within the market grounds for a calm cultural moment.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Sushi Saito (reservation essential, concierge-assisted) or, as an equally prestigious local alternative, Kyubey Ginza — a legendary omakase sushi counter a short taxi ride from Tsukiji. Experience 12–15 courses of Edomae-style sushi prepared tableside by master chefs. Return to hotel for rest after long-haul travel.

meals.breakfast: In-flight or at airport lounge upon arrival
meals.lunch: Tsukiji Outer Market street sampling — fresh tuna sashimi, tamagoyaki skewers, and clam miso soup from top market vendors
meals.dinner: Omakase dinner at Kyubey Ginza or equivalent Michelin-starred Edomae sushi restaurant in Ginza/Tsukiji area (¥30,000–¥50,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light given jet lag from long-haul flight. Confirm hotel concierge has pre-booked Day 2 and beyond reservations. Tsukiji Outer Market is most atmospheric in the early afternoon. Carry yen cash for market stalls.

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market Premium Food Tour (guided, private) — dive deep into the market with an expert local guide. Taste fresh sushi, grilled seafood, dashimaki tamago, pickled vegetables, and rare seasonal ingredients. Visit specialty tea and spice vendors. Learn about Tokyo's culinary heritage and the history of the market post-relocation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Ginza (10-minute walk or taxi) for a luxury cultural and retail experience. Visit the Itoya flagship stationery store (9 floors of premium Japanese paper, pens, and design). Explore the Ginza Six luxury mall's basement food halls (depachika) and rooftop garden. Stop at the Okamoto Taro Memorial Gallery or the Sony Park for a tech-culture preview.
day_by_day.evening: Cocktail hour at The Bar at the Mandarin Oriental Tokyo (Nihonbashi, 15-minute taxi) — stunning 37th-floor views over the city skyline. Dinner at Nihonbashi Yukari (三つ星 — three Michelin stars), celebrated for refined kaiseki-style Japanese cuisine rooted in Edo culinary tradition.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast or Tsukiji morning specialty — fresh tamago gohan (rice with raw egg) and miso soup at a local kissaten (coffee shop)
meals.lunch: Premium sushi set lunch at Sushi Dai or Daiwa Sushi within Tsukiji Outer Market (arrive early, expect a short queue even with reservation)
meals.dinner: Kaiseki dinner at Nihonbashi Yukari (¥25,000–¥40,000 per person, reservation via concierge)

day_by_day.notes: The guided Tsukiji food tour is best started by 9:00–10:00 AM for peak freshness. Ginza stores open at 11:00 AM. Mandarin Oriental Bar opens at 17:00 — ideal timing for sunset cocktails.

day_by_day.morning: Private cultural tour of Hamarikyu Gardens (5-minute taxi from Tsukiji) — a stunning Edo-period tidal garden with seasonal spring flowers (late cherry blossoms or wisteria in mid-April). Traditional matcha tea ceremony in the authentic ochaya (teahouse) on the pond island. Peaceful and immersive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scenic water bus (Tokyo Cruise) from Hamarikyu to Asakusa — a 40-minute river journey through Tokyo Bay offering unique city perspectives. Arrive at Asakusa and explore Senso-ji Temple and the Nakamise shopping arcade. Visit Kappabashi 'Kitchen Town' for premium Japanese knives, lacquerware, and ceramics as souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Imahan Asakusa — a historic sukiyaki and shabu-shabu restaurant operating since 1895, serving premium Wagyu beef in a beautifully preserved traditional setting. Post-dinner evening stroll along the Sumida River with illuminated Skytree views.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or neighborhood kissaten — Japanese morning set (toast, egg, salad, coffee) at a Tsukiji area café
meals.lunch: Tempura lunch at Daikokuya Tempura in Asakusa — a century-old institution serving crispy Edomae-style tempura over rice (tendon)
meals.dinner: Premium Wagyu sukiyaki at Imahan Asakusa (¥20,000–¥35,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Hamarikyu teahouse matcha ceremony costs extra (approx. ¥500–¥800) but is highly recommended. Water bus tickets can be purchased on-site. Asakusa is very walkable — comfortable shoes advised.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Akihabara — Tokyo's legendary Electric Town and global tech-culture hub. Private guided tour covering multi-floor electronics megastores (Yodobashi Camera, Bic Camera), retro gaming arcades, anime concept stores, and the cutting-edge maid café culture. Visit Akihabara Radio Kaikan for rare electronics and collector items.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the UDX Akihabara building and the @cosplay center. Visit the Gundam Café and Super Potato retro gaming store. Head to the BEAMS Japan concept store nearby for premium Japanese streetwear and design objects. Transfer to Ueno for a visit to the Tokyo National Museum — Japan's largest and most prestigious museum with world-class collections of samurai armor, Buddhist sculpture, and ukiyo-e prints.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in the upscale Yanaka neighborhood — a rare surviving Edo-era shitamachi (old town) district. Reserve a table at a premium kappo (counter-style) restaurant for seasonal Japanese cuisine. Evening walk through Yanaka Ginza shopping street lit by paper lanterns.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Tsukiji morning specialty
meals.lunch: Akihabara lunch at a premium Japanese curry house (e.g., Curry no Mise Akihabara) or a high-end ramen restaurant such as Fuunji (nearby Shinjuku) if routing allows
meals.dinner: Kappo-style seasonal Japanese cuisine in Yanaka or Ueno area (¥15,000–¥25,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is best explored on weekends when pedestrian zones close streets to traffic (afternoons). Tokyo National Museum closed on Mondays — Saturday is ideal. Book museum tickets in advance online.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to Shibuya and Harajuku cultural districts. Start at Meiji Jingu Shrine — a serene Shinto sanctuary set within a 70-hectare forested park. Participate in a morning purification ritual (temizu) and observe traditional wedding processions if scheduled. Walk through the forested path to Harajuku.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Omotesando — Tokyo's most architecturally distinguished boulevard lined with flagship stores by Tadao Ando (Omotesando Hills), Herzog & de Meuron (Prada), and SANAA (Dior). Visit the Nezu Museum for a world-class collection of Asian antiquities and a stunning traditional garden. Browse Comme des Garçons, Issey Miyake, and Yohji Yamamoto boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Cocktails at the rooftop bar of the Rooftop Bar Trunk Hotel (Shibuya) or the Andaz Tokyo Rooftop Bar. Dinner at Florilège (2 Michelin stars) — one of Tokyo's most celebrated contemporary French-Japanese fusion restaurants, known for its theatrical open kitchen and seasonal tasting menus.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a premium bakery brunch — Viron Boulangerie on Omotesando for French-style croissants and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Koffee Mameya or a premium café on Cat Street, Harajuku, followed by a light meal at Maisen Tonkatsu (premium pork cutlet institution on Omotesando)
meals.dinner: Contemporary French-Japanese tasting menu at Florilège, Minami-Aoyama (¥30,000–¥45,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Shrine is free to enter. Nezu Museum charges admission (approx. ¥1,300). Florilège reservations are highly competitive — book 2–3 months in advance via concierge or Tableall platform.

day_by_day.morning: Private half-day tour of teamLab Borderless (or teamLab Planets in Toyosu if Borderless is under seasonal maintenance) — Tokyo's world-famous immersive digital art museum. Experience room-scale interactive light and sound installations that redefine the boundary between technology, nature, and art. A must for tech and culture enthusiasts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Odaiba — Tokyo's futuristic artificial island. Visit the Miraikan (National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation) featuring ASIMO robot demonstrations, a walk-inside model of the Earth, and cutting-edge exhibits on AI, space, and biotechnology. Explore the DiverCity Tokyo Plaza and the life-size Gundam statue.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset views from the Odaiba seaside promenade with Rainbow Bridge and Tokyo skyline backdrop. Dinner at Ukai-tei Omotesando (transfer back to central Tokyo) — a legendary teppanyaki restaurant where master chefs prepare A5 Wagyu, lobster, and seasonal vegetables on iron griddles with theatrical precision.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium Odaiba restaurant — Tableaux in Daikanyama or a kaiseki bento at the Miraikan café
meals.dinner: A5 Wagyu teppanyaki at Ukai-tei Omotesando (¥30,000–¥50,000 per person, one of Tokyo's most celebrated teppanyaki experiences)

day_by_day.notes: teamLab venues require advance online ticket booking — slots sell out weeks ahead. Odaiba is accessible via the Yurikamome monorail from Shimbashi (scenic ride over Rainbow Bridge). Ukai-tei requires formal dress code.

day_by_day.morning: Day excursion to Nikko (2 hours by Tobu Limited Express from Asakusa) — a UNESCO World Heritage mountain shrine complex. Explore the opulent Tosho-gu Shrine, Rinno-ji Temple, and the Shinkyo Sacred Bridge. Walk through ancient cedar forests with possible late-season snow on mountain peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko's Futarasan Shrine and Taiyuin Mausoleum. Optional: brief visit to Kegon Falls (one of Japan's top three waterfalls). Enjoy the mountain scenery and crisp spring air before returning to Tokyo by early evening.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening back in Tsukiji/Ginza area. Dinner at Sazenka (2 Michelin stars) in Minami-Azabu — an extraordinary restaurant blending Chinese culinary mastery with Japanese precision and seasonal ingredients, widely regarded as one of Tokyo's most unique fine dining experiences.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Nikko yuba (tofu skin) kaiseki lunch at Meiji-no-Yakata — a historic Western-style restaurant in Nikko's national park area, famous for its yuba cuisine
meals.dinner: Chinese-Japanese fusion kaiseki at Sazenka, Minami-Azabu (¥25,000–¥40,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Depart hotel by 7:30 AM to maximize time in Nikko. Purchase Tobu Nikko All Area Pass for unlimited transportation within Nikko. Nikko can be crowded on weekends — Tuesday is ideal. Wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided cultural immersion in the Nihonbashi district — Tokyo's historic financial and cultural heart. Visit Coredo Muromachi's premium artisan shops, the Mitsukoshi flagship department store (Japan's oldest), and the Nihonbashi bridge (the zero-kilometer marker of all Japanese roads). Explore the Kite Museum (Tako no Hakubutsukan) — a quirky, fascinating collection of traditional Japanese kites.
day_by_day.afternoon: Sake tasting experience at Hasegawa Saketen (Nihonbashi) — one of Tokyo's finest sake retailers offering curated premium tastings with knowledgeable staff. Transfer to the Marunouchi district to visit the Mitsubishi Ichigokan Museum (European art in a beautifully restored 1894 red-brick building). Walk through the Marunouchi Naka-dori boulevard.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Beige Alain Ducasse Tokyo — the legendary French chef's Tokyo outpost atop the Chanel Ginza building, offering panoramic Ginza views alongside refined French haute cuisine with Japanese seasonal accents.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Tsukiji morning specialty — fresh uni (sea urchin) rice bowl at a market vendor
meals.lunch: Premium soba lunch at Yabu Soba (Kanda) — a historic 19th-century soba restaurant with tatami seating and refined hand-cut noodles
meals.dinner: French haute cuisine at Beige Alain Ducasse Tokyo, Ginza (¥30,000–¥50,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Sake tasting at Hasegawa is informal and educational — no reservation needed but arrive early. Mitsubishi Ichigokan Museum is closed on Mondays. Beige Alain Ducasse requires formal attire and advance reservation.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Shinjuku — starting with the serene Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden (one of Japan's finest landscape gardens, featuring French formal, English landscape, and Japanese traditional garden styles). In mid-to-late April, enjoy late-season cherry blossoms or vibrant spring tulips and wisteria.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the technology and innovation floors of Yodobashi Akiba (or Bic Camera Shinjuku) for the latest Japanese consumer electronics, cameras, and gadgets unavailable outside Japan. Visit the Samurai Museum in Kabukicho for an immersive experience with authentic armor, swords, and samurai history. Optional: visit the observation deck of the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building (free, panoramic views).
day_by_day.evening: Pre-dinner cocktails at the Park Hyatt Tokyo's New York Bar (made famous by Lost in Translation) on the 52nd floor — jazz performances, skyline views, and world-class cocktails. Dinner at Kozue (Park Hyatt, 40th floor) — a Michelin-recognized kaiseki restaurant with floor-to-ceiling city views and refined seasonal Japanese cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Ramen lunch at Fuunji (Shinjuku) — acclaimed for its rich tsukemen (dipping ramen) using premium dashi broth, consistently ranked among Tokyo's best
meals.dinner: Kaiseki dinner at Kozue, Park Hyatt Tokyo (¥25,000–¥40,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Shinjuku Gyoen charges a small admission fee (¥500). Alcohol is prohibited inside the garden. New York Bar has a cover charge (¥2,750 per person) waived for hotel guests. Book Kozue well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided food and culture tour of Koenji and Shimokitazawa — Tokyo's bohemian, creative neighborhoods. Explore vintage clothing stores, independent record shops, artisan coffee roasters, and local art galleries. Experience the authentic side of Tokyo's creative subculture away from tourist circuits.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Daikanyama and Nakameguro — Tokyo's most stylish residential neighborhoods. Browse the iconic Daikanyama T-Site (Tsutaya Books) — a stunning architectural bookstore complex with curated lifestyle products, vinyl records, and a premium café. Walk along the Meguro River canal (beautiful in spring with overhanging trees). Visit the Log Road Daikanyama boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Narisawa (2 Michelin stars, World's 50 Best Restaurants alumni) — one of Tokyo's most celebrated restaurants, where chef Yoshihiro Narisawa creates 'Innovative Satoyama Cuisine' inspired by Japanese nature, forests, and coastal ecosystems. A transformative fine dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a specialty coffee experience at Onibus Coffee (Nakameguro) — one of Tokyo's most respected third-wave roasters
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Ivy Place (Daikanyama T-Site) — a beautifully designed all-day restaurant with premium salads, sandwiches, and Japanese-Western fusion plates
meals.dinner: Innovative Satoyama tasting menu at Narisawa, Minami-Aoyama (¥35,000–¥55,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Narisawa is one of the hardest reservations in Tokyo — book 3+ months in advance. Daikanyama T-Site is open until 26:00 (2 AM) — ideal for an evening browse if dinner ends early. Nakameguro is most atmospheric at dusk.

day_by_day.morning: Day excursion to Hakone (90 minutes by Romancecar limited express from Shinjuku) — a stunning volcanic mountain resort area with views of Mt. Fuji (weather permitting in April). Visit the Hakone Open-Air Museum — a world-class sculpture park featuring works by Picasso, Henry Moore, and Rodin set against mountain scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ride the Hakone Ropeway over volcanic Owakudani valley (sulfuric hot springs and black eggs). Cruise across Lake Ashi on a traditional pirate ship with Mt. Fuji backdrop views. Visit the Hakone Shrine (red torii gate emerging from the lake). Optional: brief visit to the Pola Museum of Art for Impressionist masterpieces in a forest setting.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Relaxed dinner at Sushi Yoshitake (3 Michelin stars) in Ginza — an intimate 8-seat counter where master chef Masahiro Yoshitake crafts extraordinary Edomae sushi using the finest seasonal seafood, with exceptional sake pairings.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Hakone lunch at Fujiya Hotel (historic 1878 Western-style hotel in Miyanoshita) — elegant dining room with classic Japanese-Western cuisine and mountain views
meals.dinner: 3-Michelin-star Edomae sushi omakase at Sushi Yoshitake, Ginza (¥40,000–¥60,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Romancecar seats must be reserved in advance (book via Odakyu online). Hakone ropeway may be suspended in high winds — check weather. Owakudani black eggs are a local specialty (boiled in sulfuric spring water). Sushi Yoshitake requires 2–3 months advance reservation.

day_by_day.morning: Immersive morning at the Mori Art Museum (Roppongi Hills) — one of Tokyo's premier contemporary art institutions featuring cutting-edge international and Japanese artists. Combine with the Tokyo City View observation deck on the 52nd floor for 360-degree panoramic views including Mt. Fuji on clear days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Roppongi's art triangle: visit the 21_21 Design Sight (founded by Issey Miyake and Tadao Ando) in Tokyo Midtown and the National Art Center Tokyo — Japan's largest exhibition space with stunning wave-glass facade architecture by Kisho Kurokawa. Browse the Suntory Museum of Art (Japanese decorative arts) in Tokyo Midtown.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell luxury dinner at Quintessence (3 Michelin stars) in Shirokanedai — chef Shuzo Kishida's legendary French restaurant, consistently ranked among Asia's finest, offering a single prix-fixe menu of extraordinary refinement using the best French and Japanese seasonal produce. A perfect culmination of the culinary journey.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a premium brunch at bills Roppongi (Australian-style brunch institution beloved in Tokyo) — ricotta pancakes, avocado toast, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Mori Art Museum café or the Roppongi Hills Club restaurant with city views
meals.dinner: 3-Michelin-star French cuisine at Quintessence, Shirokanedai (¥40,000–¥60,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Mori Art Museum is open late (until 22:00 on most days) — the evening view from the observation deck is spectacular. 21_21 Design Sight is closed on Tuesdays. Quintessence has one of the most difficult reservations in Tokyo — book via concierge 3+ months ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo — leisurely farewell walk through Tsukiji Outer Market one last time. Purchase premium Japanese food souvenirs: high-grade matcha, artisan dashi packs, premium soy sauce, Edo Kiriko cut glass, and Japanese kitchen knives from Tsukiji's specialty stores. Visit the Tsukiji Hongan-ji Temple (a stunning Indo-Baroque Buddhist temple) for a quiet final cultural moment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time: visit the Ginza Six rooftop garden for final city views, or enjoy a final tea ceremony experience at Urasenke Tea School (Ginza branch). Check out of hotel. Private luxury car transfer to Narita or Haneda Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Tokyo. Enjoy the airport's premium lounges (JAL Sakura Lounge or ANA Suite Lounge at Haneda offer exceptional Japanese cuisine, sake, and spa facilities for premium cabin passengers).

meals.breakfast: Final Tsukiji breakfast — fresh oysters, grilled scallops, and a bowl of tuna don (tuna rice bowl) at a top market vendor
meals.lunch: Premium airport lunch at the Narita or Haneda airport premium lounge, or a final sushi meal at the airport's Sushi Saito satellite counter (Haneda) if time permits
meals.dinner: In-flight dining (business/first class) or airport lounge dinner

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for check-in and security. Haneda Airport is closer to central Tokyo (30–40 minutes by taxi). Tsukiji market vendors begin closing by midday — arrive for final shopping by 10:00 AM. Ensure all purchased food items comply with customs regulations for your destination country.
